messages.author: c6d99be19d45c603
messages.subject: Calculating measurement invariance
parts:
Dear forum,

I am trying to calculate measurment invariance.
My data includes two groups.

I found the code:
measurementInvariance(model = model_configMI,
                      data = data_both,
                      group = "GP")

Actually, I expected to get the same results as if i test the models against each other by myself. I set up the four models by using the SchroedersGnambs2020 suggestions using reference group (see their Supplement).
However, the metric model (set up by myself) seems to be different to the loadings model (automatically set up in the above code).

These are the results:
Chi-Squared Difference
Test Df AIC BIC Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)
fit.configural 1110 37766 39002 2391.0
fit.loadings 1146 37731 38816 2428.4 37.390 36 0.40512
fit.intercepts 1182 37716 38649 2484.9 56.563 36 0.01584 *
fit.means 1182 37716 38649 2484.9 0.000 0

versus
lavTestLRT(fit_config, fit_metric, method="satorra.bentler.2010")
Df AIC BIC Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)
fit_config 1110 37766 39002 2391.0
fit_metric 1146 37857 38941 2554.1 87.808 36 3.22e-06 ***

I wonder which is the better option?
Additionally, my fits are not very good. Considering that the model includes many df the fit is not bad either (and far better than e.g. a single factor model). Is it valid to calculate such difference tests even if the fits are not perfect?

Thanks for any advice,
Stephan

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Calculating measurement invariance
parts:
Stephan,

Answering the last point--the likelihood ratio (difference) test only follows the chi-squared distribution if the full model fits perfectly. So while you may accept the full model without good fit (which is an entirely different discussion), you should be aware the p-value for the difference test is going to be incorrect.

Pat

There was no attachment.
However, the metric model (set up by myself) seems to be different to the loadings model (automatically set up in the above code).

They have the same df but different chi-squared values, so they are not equivalent.  You can check what makes them different by comparing their summary() output to see which parameters were (not) estimated in each model.  measurementInvariance() returns a list of lavaan objects that you can assign to an object (e.g., "out"), then extract the list elements by name

out[["fit.loadings"]]
